name: Places SDK for Android

dataTypes.type: App info and performance / Crash logs
dataTypes.when: Always: stack traces for crashes within the SDK code and crash metrics such as abnormal terminations.
Always: request metadata including device metadata (OS version, name, model, brand, form factor), SDK build/version, API usage and number of results returned.

dataTypes.type: Device or other IDs / Device or other IDs
dataTypes.when: Always: a Google Maps Platform SDK identifier specific to the app, used to measure daily active SDK users.
Only if the app uses features that discover the place at the device's current location (e.g. current place): lat/lng coordinates and nearby WiFi access points are collected.
Only if the app uses UI components such as the Places Autocomplete widgets: widget interaction data.

ask: Do you call current-place / nearby-from-device-location features? If no, remove Location / Precise location.
Do you set country codes or lat/lng bounds (location bias/restriction) derived from the user's location? If yes, consider declaring Location / Approximate location for that.

Users' typed Autocomplete queries are sent to Google as API input parameters. Decide whether to declare App activity / In-app search history (Google's page lists 'input parameters for Places APIs' as request metadata but does not map it to a Play type).
Do you also use the Maps SDK? Declare the google-maps entry too.

sources.title: Prepare for Google Play's data disclosure requirements (Places SDK for Android)

notes: Google's Places page lists the items but does not state whether data is shared, whether location is processed ephemerally, or which Play purposes apply. Purposes, shared=false and ephemeral=false are our interpretation; hence medium confidence. IP address is also collected ('to understand SDK usage and improve Google services'); not mapped since Play has no IP data type and the page does not say it is used for location. places-compat is the deprecated compatibility library on Google Maven; places-ktx and places-compose (com.google.maps.android) wrap the Places SDK.
